newsitem.title: ITALY: BOXING-THOUSANDS TURN OUT FOR ITALIAN BOXER'S BURIAL.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-THOUSANDS TURN OUT FOR ITALIAN BOXER'S BURIAL.

text.p: Several thousand mourners turned out on Wednesday for the funeral of Italian boxer Fabrizio De Chiara who died after being knocked out during an Italian title fight.
Vincenzo Imparato, De Chiara's opponent in Saturday's middleweight bout, helped to carry the coffin to the packed church in De Chiara's home town, near Milan.

More than a thousand people thronged the streets outside. Friends of the boxer, who had just turned 25, put up a banner reading "You'll never walk alone" -- the title of a song often sung by fans at English sports events -- outside De Chiara's house.

Four funeral cars were needed to carry the dozens of wreaths sent from friends and Italian sporting associations, including the national squad for which De Chiara fought in the Barcelona Olympics in 1992. He turned professional two years ago.
De Chiara's trainer in Barcelona, Franco Falcinelli, recalled him as someone "who always gave his all".
"Only heroes behave like that," he said.

De Chiara's death has prompted renewed criticism of boxing and calls for the sport to be banned. Saturday's fight was stopped mid-way through the 12th round after Imparato landed two sharp blows to De Chiara's head followed by one to the stomach.
Imparato was devastated when De Chiara collapsed in a coma and died in hospital less than 24 hours later. He said he thought the fight should have been stopped in the 11th round.
Magistrates have opened an investigation into the death.
